_doc.purpose: The recorded misfire shapes plus two positive controls, used to prove lib/core/arbitration.cjs's resolveArbitration suppresses the enforcement misfires the 2026-07-02 WATCH item documented, without ever licensing a constitutional floor to be dropped.
_doc.source_file: /home/jsagi/.claude/projects/-home-jsagi/memory/feedback_1_15_enforcement_regression_watch.md -- this file lives outside this repository, under the navigator's own Claude Code project memory directory, not the repo tree. It can be edited, moved or absent on another machine, which is exactly why every fixture below carries a verbatim source_quote rather than a paraphrase: the quote embedded here cannot drift even if the source file does.
_doc.provenance_rule: Every fixture's source_quote is copied verbatim, byte-for-byte, from source_file. Never paraphrased, never summarized, never re-worded.
_doc.reconstruction_limitation: These fixtures are shapes reconstructed from a prose incident log (the WATCH memory file), not captured conversation transcripts; no 2026-07 transcripts exist anywhere in this repo or its memory directory, and the sessions are two months past. They prove the arbiter's logic holds against the recorded failure modes described in that log. They do not prove the persona regression itself closed in live use. The only honest close on that second claim is a fresh WATCH window observed after this phase ships, not a replay against fixtures derived from the original complaint.
_doc.count_derivation: Enumerated by one fixture per distinct (date, mechanism, turn-context) triple, reading the WATCH file directly rather than the research summary's own transcription table. The WATCH file's 4th-instance paragraph names two distinct misfires (the F.1 stale-artifact gate firing on 6+ consecutive turns of one command-inventory conversation, and a separate room-binding F.8 gate firing on an unrelated Desktop-upload question); both are kept as two rows because their turn-context differs, but the 6+ consecutive F.1 fires WITHIN that same conversation are collapsed into ONE row, one shape, not six, since they share date, mechanism and context. No incident was split beyond what the source text itself already separates, and none was padded to reach any target count.
_doc.count_discrepancy_note: The planning brief states '7 incidents / 9 misfires'. Enumerating the WATCH file directly under the rule above yields 8 distinct fixtures (three from the first live-proof-of-mechanism session, two from the 4th-instance paragraph, and one each from the 5th instance, the 2026-07-08 instance and the 2026-07-12 instance), one fewer than the brief's stated 9. This is recorded as the finding rather than padded to match: the likeliest source of the brief's higher count is treating the 4th instance's 6+ consecutive F.1 fires as more than one shape, which the count-honesty rule above forbids.
